CheckTitle: Ensure iam:PassRole grants are restricted by iam:PassedToService or resource tag conditions
Description: Policies granting iam:PassRole on Resource: * without iam:PassedToService or aws:ResourceTag/* conditions allow a principal to pass any role — including high-privilege roles — to any AWS service. This is a documented IAM privilege escalation vector: a low-privilege identity with unrestricted iam:PassRole can instantiate a service (e.g., EC2 instance, Lambda function) that assumes an admin role on its behalf.
Risk: Unrestricted iam:PassRole allows privilege escalation via service instantiation. An attacker with iam:PassRole and ec2:RunInstances can pass an admin role to a new EC2 instance and use its instance profile to perform privileged operations. This vector is explicitly documented in the AWS IAM documentation section on granting permissions to pass a role.
Remediation: Add iam:PassedToService conditions to restrict PassRole to specific target services (e.g., ec2.amazonaws.com, lambda.amazonaws.com). Alternatively, add aws:ResourceTag/* conditions to restrict which roles can be passed by attribute. If possible, restrict the Resource element to specific role ARNs instead of using Resource: *.
SeverityBasis: AWS IAM documentation explicitly documents iam:PassRole as a privilege escalation vector when used without conditions; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 AC-6 (Least Privilege), CM-5 (Access Restrictions for Change). High severity reflects that exploitation requires only a companion service-instantiation permission alongside iam:PassRole.
AuthoritativeSource: AWS IAM documentation — Granting a user permissions to pass a role to an AWS service; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
CISControl: N/A — PassRole condition enforcement is not individually enumerated in CIS AWS 3.0.0
ThreatReference: Security research on IAM privilege escalation paths via iam:PassRole + service instantiation (widely documented in cloud security literature)
